title: Energy bills to rise by 26% from January after gas prices surge
summary:
Energy bills will soar by 26% for millions of households in January after a surge in gas prices sparked by the Iran war.
A typical bill will increase by about £37 a month in the first three months of the new year, although the price will depend on how much energy a household uses, so it could be closer to £60 extra a month in winter.
A household using a typical amount of energy in England, Scotland and Wales and paying by direct debit, would see their annual bill rise from £1,723 to £2,166 if the increase was sustained for a year, said regulator Ofgem.
The government will pay millions of households £100 from 4 January to help cover winter costs on top of an existing VAT cut on electricity.

title: The Iowa Lead Detonation Happened. Now the Real Work Begins to Study It
summary:
On Wednesday morning, the US Army detonated nearly five tons of degraded lead azide outside of Middletown, Iowa.
Air, soil, and water samples they’ve collected will determine the extent of lead exposure, if any, in Middletown and the surrounding area.
Poor communication between the Army and towns in the path of the fallout led to a public uproar.
Several departments at the University of Iowa kicked into gear to begin to set up air and soil monitoring stations late last week.
Scientists at Purdue University, nearly 300 miles away, also put out a call for soil samples from Middletown.

title: Energy price cap: The Iran war is being blamed for raising bills - here's why
summary:
Ofgem estimates that around £404 of the £443 increase in the annual energy price cap from January is due to higher wholesale natural gas prices.
Natural gas is used for heating by around 85% of homes, according to trade body Energy UK, and by power companies to generate electricity.
This means that when the wholesale price of gas rises, its feeds directly into the costs British households pay when they use either gas or electricity.
While the price of gas puts pressure on energy bills, other costs including upgrading the electricity grid to cope with more sources of renewable generation, feed into what households pay.
However, Ofgem says that these additional costs made no contribution to the rise in bills in the latest period.

title: Floating nature islands installed in Glasgow parks as Games legacy
summary:
Floating islands are being installed on ponds in five of Glasgow's parks as part of the 2026 Commonwealth Games legacy.
The islands, which are being planted by community groups, are designed to encourage wildlife and help clean the water.
The project will create almost 250 square metres of new wildlife habitat which is expected to last about 20 years.
Glasgow 2026 organisers say they are funding the projects as part of their commitment to greener games.

title: Med Emre: Diesel tanker carrying tonnes capsizes near Ibiza, killing one
summary:
An oil tanker carrying up to 7,000 tonnes of diesel has capsized off the coast of Ibiza, leaving one crew member dead, authorities have said.
The Med Emre, a Malta-flagged vessel, was carrying 17 crew members who were all rescued.
Earlier, regional emergencies director Pablo Gárriz said the tanker had not completely sunk, as had originally been reported.
The Med Emre capsized 25 nautical miles (46 km; 29 miles) from Ibiza's coastline and 57 nautical miles from Valencia.
The chemical tanker was en route from Algeciras, in southern Spain, to Barcelona in the north-east.

title: As food prices rise, do shoppers still care about sustainability?
summary:
One economist told Bloomberg that Americans should expect food prices to keep creeping up into next year.
With food prices creeping up, it’s worth asking whatever happened to the idea of consumers as climate or environmental activists.
But do today’s shoppers still care about where their food comes from and how it’s grown when they’re worried about their supermarket bill (and all the other ones)?
“People want a sustainable option.
Real change may come when policy changes and public investment in sustainable food systems matches consumer desires, said Jody Kirchner, director of market insights at Good Food Institute, a think tank focused on the alternative protein economy.
